newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close down on blue-chip losses.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close down on blue-chip losses.

text.p: Jakarta shares price closed down on Monday following foreign-led selling of selected market heavyweights, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index felll 2.04 points, or 0.35 percent, to 586.31 points after hitting a day high of 591.88. Losers led gainers by 65 to 49, with 54 counters unchanged.
Brokers said market was likely to be weak on Tuesday since Friday's rise in the Dow Jones and strong regional markets had failed to spur fresh buying due to negative news on some heavyweights.
The falls in the heavweights coupled with profit-taking on some small-capitalised stocks had brought down the index in the afternoon session, brokers said.

Heavyweight Sampoerna fell 1,325 rupiah, or 5.9 percent to 21,125 rupiah on a volume of 463,500 shares after news that Moody's had placed $200 million in notes issued by a subsidiary on review for a possible downgrade, brokers said.

Brokers said the news of the possible downgrade came as Sampoerna announced it had secured a fresh short-term bank facility of $400 million, and they were confused about why the company was seeking fresh funds.

Cement producers, including Semen Gresik and Semen Cibinong, were among the losers after news that the trade and industry had forecast that production would exceed demand in 1997 and 1998, brokers said.
Confectionery manufacturer Mayora Indah topped the active list with 6.6 million shares traded, but fell 25 rupiah to 1,050 rupiah on what brokers said was profit-taking after earlier gains.
It rose to 1,100 rupiah earlier on market talk of possible acquisitions and a link-up with a foreign partner.

Timber firm Barito Pacific also fell on profit-taking. It lost 50 rupiah to 1,475 on a volume of 6.4 million shares after a company official denied rumours that President Suharto's daughter was planning to buy a stake in the company. It rose to 1,600 rupiah in early trade on the rumours.
